title: Quick check: Working with Existing React Applications

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Working with Existing React Applications”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Understanding unfamiliar code belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Understanding unfamiliar code belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Working with Existing React Applications: Understanding unfamiliar code belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Understanding unfamiliar code?
options: Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Working with Existing React Applications: Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Working with Existing React Applications” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Working with Existing React Applications: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
